evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` check only requires changed positive manager PIDs and changed nonempty invocation IDs; it never verifies that the before/after manager snapshots are on the same guest boot. A reboot between those snapshots can change both manager identifiers and make `manager_restarted` true without isolating a manager restart. The separate `boot_id_changed` check does not gate this result. Requiring equal, nonempty boot IDs here is a routine correctness fix, not a new approval or protection requirement.
